public_payload.normalized_proposition: Anthropic raised $75 billion in 2026 so far, and both OpenAI and Anthropic lowered gross margin projections at the end of 2025.

statement.excerpt: Despite its so-called profitability, Anthropic has had to raise a combined $75 billion (between Google, Amazon and investors) since the beginning of the year. Both OpenAI and Anthropic had to lower their gross margin projections at the end of 2025.

from_speaker: since the beginning of the year
our_interpretation: Fundraising covers January 1 through May 26, 2026. The ordinary reading of 'has had to raise' is completed fundraising, excluding unexercised conditional future investments and avoiding double counting.
Interpret 'at the end of 2025' as the final calendar quarter of 2025. Compare forecasts for the same future period under the same gross-margin definition.
Treat 'had to' as descriptive emphasis unless evidence identifies a separate claim of financial necessity.
The fundraising sentence supplies no reporting or accounting basis, so its contract basis remains unknown. The linked gross-margin discussion concerns press-reported estimates.

The single metric_scope records the quantified fundraising assertion. The gross-margin assertions require separate company-specific comparisons and cannot be substituted for evidence of the funding total.
criteria.support_condition: A complete, nonduplicated closing record establishes approximately $75 billion raised by May 26, and dated comparable forecasts establish downward gross-margin revisions by both companies during Q4 2025.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A complete comparable funding record establishes a materially different total, or dated forecast records show that either alleged Q4 revision did not occur. Announced future financing is not evidence of completed fundraising.

evidence.explanation: This establishes one announced funding component, not a complete year-to-date total. Its company-reported round amount cannot establish the claim's unspecified aggregate basis.
The announcement explicitly separates an immediate investment from potential later funding. Counting the entire possible amount as already raised would erase that distinction.

The opening paragraph reports an initial Google investment of at least $10 billion, potentially rising to $40 billion if performance targets are met. This is a report of financing terms, not proof that the full potential amount had been received.

evidence.locator: Section “Soaring inference costs squeeze profit margins”
evidence.explanation: This reports lower OpenAI margin expectations in a February account of revised forecasts. It does not establish that the revision occurred at the end of 2025, and it concerns a different metric from Anthropic fundraising.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A dated, nonduplicated funding reconciliation through May 26 and both companies' comparable forecast versions showing when the gross-margin reductions were made.
